question: What will be the monthly change in US nonfarm payrolls (BLS) for August 2026, as first published?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the first published value of the monthly change in US nonfarm payrolls (BLS) for August 2026 (FRED series PAYEMS, diff). Later revisions are ignored.
research:
The latest official figure, for July 2026, was a fall of 23k. The August figure comes out on Friday, 2026-09-04. Several search results were published after 2026-08-28, and I left all of them out.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the first-print change in FRED PAYEMS for August 2026. That number comes from the BLS Employment Situation release, which I expect on 2026-09-04 at 8:30 ET (the first Friday, which fits the question's resolution timing). I could not fetch BLS or FRED directly because the proxy refused the connection.
- 2026-08-07: The latest published value is July 2026 at **-23k**, with unemployment at 4.1%. [BLS archive](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_08072026.htm); [BLS TED](https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/little-change-in-nonfarm-payroll-employment-in-july-2026.htm)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The August report had not been published as of 2026-08-28.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-28: In his Jackson Hole keynote, Fed Chair Warsh called the labor market "broadly resilient" and at full employment. He said inflation is too high (PCE 3.7% over the past year) and that softer job gains reflect demographics. [Kpler](https://www.kpler.com/es/blog/warsh-takes-a-hawkish-tone-at-jackson-hole); [Lord Abbett](https://www.lordabbett.com/en-us/financial-advisor/insights/markets-and-economy/2026/jackson-hole-2026-four-takeaways-for-investors.html)
- 2026-08-27: Initial jobless claims fell to 203k for the week ending Aug 22, the lowest since October 2022, against a 208k consensus. Continuing claims were about 1.8M, which points to slow hiring but few layoffs. [PNC](https://www.pnc.com/content/dam/pnc-com/pdf/aboutpnc/EconomicReports/EconomicUpdates/2026/PNC_Economics_Research_Claims_27_August_2026.pdf); [ROIC](https://www.roic.ai/news/us-jobless-claims-fall-again-labor-market-shows-resilience-08-27-2026)
- 2026-08-25: ADP's weekly NER Pulse showed private employers adding an average of 11,750 jobs a week over the four weeks to Aug 8, up from 9,500. That is the second straight weekly rise after a seven-week slide. [Barchart/ADP](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/4020506/adp-national-employment-report-preliminary-estimate-for-august-8-2026); [SIA](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/private-sector-hiring-grows-for-second-week)
- 2026-08-20: Claims were 206k for the week ending Aug 15, with a 4-week average of 204k. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-20/us-weekly-jobless-claims-edged-lower-to-206-000-in-latest-week); [Quartz](https://qz.com/us-jobless-claims-weekly-august-15-2026-082026)
- 2026-08-07: July details:
  - Consensus was +83k and the actual was -23k.
  - Government fell 53k, mostly local government education. Economists said this was largely a seasonal effect that could be revised away.
  - Private payrolls rose 30k, and leisure and hospitality fell 40k.
  - May was revised down 66k to +63k, and June down 37k to +20k.
  - The fall in unemployment to 4.1% came from lower labor force participation.
  
  [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/here-are-three-key-takeaways-from-the-disappointing-july-jobs-report.html); [NAM](https://nam.org/nonfarm-payrolls-fell-23000-in-july-as-unemployment-edged-down-to-4-1/); [Quartz](https://qz.com/us-payrolls-july-2026-jobs-report-080726); [Indeed](https://hiringlab.indeed.com/2026/08/07/july-2026-jobs-report-unexpected-turbulence/)

## 4. Base rates
- First prints in 2026, as far as I could find:
  - January: +130k (report delayed by a shutdown). [Chase](https://www.chase.com/personal/investments/learning-and-insights/article/january-2026-jobs-report-130000-new-jobs-slightly-lower-unemployment)
  - February: about -92k, held down by a strike. This may be a revised figure rather than the first print. [Trading Economics](https://www.tradingeconomics.com/united-states/non-farm-payrolls/news/524890)
  - May: reported as +172k, but I could not confirm that was the first print.
  - June: +57k. [FT Portfolios](https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/7/2/nonfarm-payrolls-rose-57,000-in-june)
  - July: -23k.
- I could not confirm first prints for March and April.
- After revisions, the May to July three-month average is about +20k.
- Breakeven job growth is now estimated at about 0 to 50k a month because immigration is low: around 40k from RBC (2025) and about 50k from Goldman Sachs. [RBC](https://www.rbc.com/en/economics/us-analysis/us-featured-analysis/us-breakeven-employment-is-falling/); [Kolko](https://jedkolko.substack.com/p/updated-breakeven-rate-for-monthly)
- First prints swing a lot from month to month. In 2026 they ranged from about -92k to +172k, and the gap between consensus and the actual number is often 50 to 100k (July missed by 106k).
- If July's government drop was really a seasonal distortion, it could reverse in August. August first prints have historically tended to come in weak and get revised up later. This is general knowledge; I did not verify it with a 2026 source.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Dow Jones, Bloomberg or LSEG consensus for August published on or before 2026-08-28. Those surveys usually come out in the week of the release.
- A Kalshi article said traders were pricing about +43k, compared with an economist expectation of about 65k. I could not confirm its publication date. [Kalshi News](https://news.kalshi.com/p/august-jobs-report-forecast-traders-are-pricing-43-000-jobs-added)
- The Kalshi market ticker is KXPAYROLLS-26AUG. I could not get a dated price from on or before Aug 28. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/api/public/market/KXPAYROLLS-26AUG-T0?depth=true)
- I found no Polymarket or Manifold prices.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-09-01: ISM manufacturing employment index.
- About 2026-09-02: JOLTS for July.
- About 2026-09-02: ADP National Employment Report for August.
- 2026-09-03: Weekly jobless claims and ISM services employment.
- 2026-09-04: BLS Employment Situation for August, which resolves the question.
- Beyond the release itself, the main things that could move the number are:
  - whether July's seasonal drop in government education jobs reverses
  - the August survey response rate
  - any strike effects

The dates in this section are the usual release schedule. I did not confirm them for 2026.
